items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: There was Chris Kelly, a great trumpet player. It was funky. Had a following. A lot of people liked his music.

ctx.x: . . . with a gun and stuff, and he smashed . . . All the musicians ran. Jumped out the window, and he smashed all the instruments. Bunk’s trumpet was on the chair or something, and it got smashed up. Let me ask you this, Mr. Barker. You . . . Who were some of the better that you heard in New Orleans before you, before the ’20s, before you were a kid? Like some of the better clarinet players and trombone players.

There was a gang of them. Adolphe Alexander played the [expletive deleted] out the clarinet, but he never was featured. Hell of a musician. There was Alexander’s family. He had two brothers. One played drums. One played piano. The old man played baritone horn with my grandfather in the Onward Brass Band. There was Chris Kelly, a great trumpet player. It was funky. Had a following. A lot of people liked his music. At night he played a funky blues, nine different blues in nine different tempos. He played yard…
Did he end up playing bass?

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: Or you saw Chris Kelly on a truck, playing them Blues.

ctx.x: None of them people. This was who was... Mister Manuel Perez, when he'd blow that trumpet...cornet in the street, and everybody said, "That's Mister Manuel Perez blowing." Or you saw Chris Kelly on a truck, playing them Blues. You'd say, "I'd like to do that." You'd see how them people get affected by that music. You'd say, "Mister Chris really blows. Did you hear him play? Yeah, Mister
Who would be in some of the bands?

Well, as I, as I was gonna know them, that was Chris Keller's band, it was Walter Blue's band, it was Buddy Petit's band, Joe Petit's Columbia, Columbia band, it was Longhead Bob's band, the Maple Leaf, Leaf band, Emanuel Perez's band, Hippolyte Charles' band, that was that, that was the Silver Maple Leaf band.
Who was involved with the Blues band? Do you remember any of those guys?

items.title: Danny Barker Interview, 1959-06-18
items.q: He used to play Chris Kelly's Love in harmony

ctx.x: And it's a wonderful jazz man to hear the way he does the two horns, you know? Sure is.
He used to play Chris Kelly's Love in harmony, and then play the variations and everything. That's old slow driving. Yes. You know who that is? No I don't. And Cook. You still living?
